title: Observability translation guide for product metrics and trace owners
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a pragmatic translation guide to help product/product-ops owners and runtime/ops (trace) owners speak the same observability language. The goal is to reduce handoffs, speed investigations, and make dashboard changes lower-risk when we change model rollout, caching, or routing policies.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Common product-facing metrics we export (per-route latencies, perceived latency, user error rate, freshness).
- How those metrics map to trace anchors and span tags operators need to debug fast.
- Lightweight sampling and trace-labeling conventions for multi-hop inference where model fan-out and sidecars exist.
- Dashboard gating rules: when a panel should be product-visible vs operator-only.
- A short rollout checklist for panel pruning and signal retirement.

Quick rules of thumb (for product owners):
- If a product SLI has >3 upstream causes, it needs a trace anchor and a companion operator panel. Don’t expect metric-only drilldowns to be sufficient.
- Product SLIs should prefer 95th/99th quantiles for user experience metrics; operator panels should expose full quantile curves + heatmaps for debugging.
- Add a single canonical example query (and example trace id) in the panel notes that demonstrates a failure mode — saves 10–30m per incident.

Metric → Trace mapping examples (concrete):
1) Per-route tail latency (user-facing 99p TTFB):
   - Product metric: route.latency.ms.p99 (tagged by route, model-version, region)
   - Trace anchor: span type = request.proxy -> annotate spans with kvcache.hit=true/false, model.call=true/false, backend.queue_ms
   - Operator needs: session_id, warm_start boolean, kv_prefetch_hit_ratio, model_name, model_variant, hardware_type

2) Prefix warmth / KV cache cold-starts: 
   - Product metric: route.kv_warmth.p50/p95 (fraction of requests with cached prefix)
   - Trace anchor: prefix.prefetch span (duration, prefix.size, ttl_bucket)
   - Operator tags: eviction_reason, tenant_weight, memory_pressure_bucket

3) Model fallback rate (automatic fallback to quantized or smaller model):
   - Product metric: route.model_fallback.rate (per-minute)
   - Trace anchor: routing.policy_eval span (policy_id, fallback_target)
   - Operator signals: capacity_tier, mem_used_percent, model_load_ms

Span and tag conventions (proposal):
- span.service: one of {ingest-proxy, router, kvcache, model-worker, aggregator}
- span.op: short op name (e.g., model_infer, kv_lookup, batch_pack)
- common tags: request.id, session.id, route, tenant.id, model.name, model.variant, hw.type, kv.hit (true|false), fallback (none|quantized|smaller)
- annotate sampling hints: sample.hint=investigate if route.latency.ms > 3x baseline or fallback.rate > threshold

Sampling policy (lightweight and cost-aware):
- Default: 0.5% of all requests for full traces, biased sampling that increases to 5% for requests hitting tail-latency or fallback conditions.
- Always sample 100% of requests that trigger a canary or rollback flag (rollout=canary).
- Keep one persistent sample per 10k requests per route-model combination to build historical examples.

Dashboard gating: product vs operator panels
- Product-visible panels (console home for product teams):
  - High-level SLIs (p50/p95/p99 latency, success rate, fallback rate) with simple annotations for recent rollouts.
  - Cost view: tokens per route, avg tokens per request, gross token spend per day (rolling 30d).
- Operator-only panels (sre/engineers):
  - Span-level heatmaps, kv-eviction timelines, model load latencies, hardware saturation metrics, per-worker queue length.
- If an operator-only panel becomes essential for product troubleshooting, create a curated product view (subset) with explanatory notes and an example trace.

Panel pruning and retirement checklist (when removing or consolidating panels):
- Owners declare intent on panel:owner slate and add to a 2-week pruning window.
- Confirm there are no active runbooks referencing the panel (search for panel id in runbooks).
- Add a 30-day ramp: hide from default product dashboards, keep operator access, and post a note in #obs-announce.
- After 30 days, remove or merge; record the change in the telemetry-change-log (confluence).

Investigation playbook (short):
1) Start at product SLI. If p99 jumps, check recent rollouts and capacity changes (console rollouts tab).
2) Look for correlated fallback.rate or kv_warmth drop. If present, jump to operator panel and find a representative trace id.
3) Use trace to answer: did we hit model load latency? is batching delayed? is kv lookup slow or eviction heavy?
4) If trace ambiguous, bump sampling hint for that route and capture 1k traces then schedule a short postmortem run.

Unresolved questions / tradeoffs (open):
- How long to persist 100% traces for SRE hotpaths vs cost constraints? proposal: 7 days hot storage, 90 days archived with aggregated summaries.
- Should product panels expose per-tenant kv_warmth? privacy / cost tradeoffs — currently gated to operator dashboards.
- Automating panel pruning: can we add a telemetry metric for "panel-use-count" so owners have data when deciding to prune? (JIRA OBS-4123 ticket)

Action items / next steps:
- Arielle to prototype sample.hint tagging in router (PR: github:repo/observability-telemetry#142) by 2026-01-20.
- Jordan to add example trace ids and product-friendly notes to top 5 product panels by 2026-02-02.
- Samir to run a 2-week panel-pruning pilot for low-use dashboards (start 2026-02-09).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the translation tight: product owners want short narratives + one example trace; operators want spans + tags.
- Avoid adding too many quantiles to product dashboards — prefer 95/99 and link to operator view for deep dives.
- Save a few 'canonical' failure traces per route-model in a small search index for quick repro.

References and bookmarks:
- Slack: #obs-instrumentation thread 'kv-eviction-hotpath' (link pinned in channel)
- Confluence: OBS-translate-2025 (design doc)
- JIRA: OBS-4123 (panel pruning automation)

If you're reading this as a product owner: flag any panel you rely on and add the example trace id (how-to: open panel -> edit -> meta -> example_trace_id).
If you're an operator: add the span.samples example to the operator panel so product owners can link straight into representative traces.

End of note.
